purpose: Real but brief, controlled, fully-reversed stop/start qualification of all three production transfer_index writers, individually and combined. No cutover, no permanent quiesce.

stop.lsof_check_after: no handle for pid 21076 on the DB file

start.log_check: stdout (listener.log) showed normal birth/detection events resuming immediately; stderr (listener_err.log) had zero 'database is locked'/'database is busy' occurrences in the restart-window tail -- prior 'locked' occurrences found via grep were historical, located ~24,000 lines earlier in the log (line ~149207 of 173775 total), well before this test window, and represent the app's own working retry-with-backoff mechanism (DB_RETRY messages), not a new condition caused by this test.

creator_funding_worker.checkpoint_mechanism: Fully DB-backed via creator_funding_queue.status column (pending/retry/running/complete/failed/expired), queried fresh on each poll cycle -- confirmed via source read of src/core/creator_funding_worker.py (lines ~528, ~561, ~645-763, ~1847-1904). No in-memory-only or file-based checkpoint exists; a stop/start cannot lose or duplicate queued work by construction, since the next poll simply re-selects rows still in pending/retry state.

stop.note: Longer than listener's stop -- consistent with the worker waiting out its current in-flight extraction call before exiting gracefully, not a hang (supervisor reported clean 'stopped', no force-kill needed).
stop.note_on_running_1: The 'running=1' row was NOT reset/orphaned by the stop -- see restart verification below, which shows normal continued progress from this state, not a stuck/duplicated row.

start.resume_correctness: retry 29->28 and running 1->2 shows the worker resumed normal drain/pickup from persisted state -- no duplication (complete/expired/failed counts unchanged, meaning no re-processing of already-terminal rows), no work lost (pending count held steady at 18, consistent with organic replenishment matching drain rate).
start.log_check: No 'database is locked'/'database is busy' in creator_funding_worker.log or _err.log during the restart window. One pre-existing unrelated error ('Error in classify_addresses_from_funding: no such table: creator_funders') present before and after the test, unrelated to lock/quiesce behavior -- flagged as a pre-existing application condition, not caused by or relevant to this qualification.

watchtower_api.distinguishing_note: This is a full supervisorctl STOP/START (process termination + fresh spawn), NOT a Gunicorn SIGHUP reload. SIGHUP reloads workers in-place without guaranteeing termination of already-spawned daemon threads; a STOP guarantees full process (and therefore thread) death. This test exercised STOP/START only, consistent with the real P5B cutover's actual quiesce mechanism.

pre_stop.in_flight_extraction_thread: None expected/observed -- toggle is false, and no extraction endpoint was invoked during this test, consistent with the milestone's own framing that this specific property (thread survives process death) could not be positively exercised live without arming the toggle, which was correctly not done.

stop.note: Matches the configured graceful_timeout of 10s, consistent with Gunicorn waiting out its graceful shutdown window as expected.
stop.full_gunicorn_process_scan_after: ps aux | grep gunicorn returned zero matches
stop.health_check_after_stop: curl to :5002 returned exit code 7 (connection refused) / HTTP code 000 -- confirms port fully unbound, no listener remains

start.auto_extract_funders_toggle_after_restar: false -- UNCHANGED, confirms stop/start does not accidentally flip app-level DB state
start.log_check: logs/supervisor/api_err.log tail showed zero 'database is locked'/'database is busy'/traceback occurrences in the restart window.

combined_quiesce_test.stop_order_rationale: watchtower_api stopped first because it is the sole entry point that could arm NEW extraction work (via the toggle-flip + trigger routes) while the other two are still running; stopping it first eliminates any possibility of new work being queued during the remainder of the shutdown sequence. creator_funding_worker stopped second to drain/halt its own already-queued work before finally stopping watchtower_listener, which is the primary ingestion source feeding new rows into creator_funding_queue in the first place -- stopping it last minimizes the window where new work could be created with no worker able to pick it up (though even that is harmless by design, since the DB-backed queue checkpoint tolerates this).
combined_quiesce_test.start_order_rationale: Reverse of stop order. Listener started first so it is immediately ready to catch new pump.fun WS events and begin populating creator_funding_queue again. creator_funding_worker started second so it can begin draining any queue growth from the listener as soon as it resumes. watchtower_api started last since it is the highest-risk re-arming surface (toggle-flip + trigger routes) and there is no operational need for it to be first; starting it last does not delay any other service's readiness.

start_timestamps_utc.all_three_confirmed_running_and_stable: 2026-08-20T18:02:35Z (checked again after +15s stability window, all still RUNNING with growing uptime, no restart)

combined_quiesce_test.verdict: PASS -- all three quiesced cleanly in dependency-safe order, all three restarted cleanly in reverse dependency-safe order, no crash loops, no lock errors, no lost/duplicated work.

measured_downtime_summary.combined_zero_writer_interval_note: Measured from all-three-confirmed-STOPPED (18:01:02Z) to restart-begin (18:02:07Z) = 65s. This is the actual measured 'all three simultaneously down' window used for the zero-writer proof polling in the companion artifact.

real_cutover_downtime_extrapolation.zero_writer_proof_window_real: ~10-15s (a real cutover only needs to hold the zero-writer state long enough to run the multi-signal check once, not the full 65s exploratory window used here)
real_cutover_downtime_extrapolation.delta_copy_and_identity_reconciliation_a: NOT re-benchmarked in this R1 -- reference the P5A artifacts (docs/audits/storage_lifecycle_p5a_part*.json) for those already-measured portions, since this milestone's scope is the writer-quiesce mechanics only, not the DB-file-level cutover operations.
real_cutover_downtime_extrapolation.rough_total_estimate: quiesce (~26s) + zero-writer proof (~15s) + [P5A-benchmarked delta/reconciliation/switch time] + restart (~25s) + first-new-write confirmation (variable, minutes) = quiesce/restart portion alone is well under 2 minutes; total real-cutover downtime is dominated by whatever the P5A-benchmarked delta-copy/reconciliation/switch duration is, not by the writer-quiesce mechanics qualified here.

in_flight_work_proof.listener: Cannot write -- confirmed fully stopped (process gone, no lsof handle) during the entire combined-down window.
in_flight_work_proof.creator_funding_worker: No surviving work process during combined-down window (confirmed stopped); its queued/in-progress work is durable in creator_funding_queue.status and was proven (individual test above) to resume correctly rather than being lost or duplicated on restart.
in_flight_work_proof.watchtower_api_daemon_threads: Python daemon threads (threading.Thread(daemon=True)) are, by Python's own runtime semantics, terminated unconditionally when their parent process exits -- this is inherent behavior, not something that needs separate live verification once the process itself is confirmed fully gone (Part 5's ps aux scan showed zero gunicorn processes of any kind after stop). Since auto_extract_funders was 'false' throughout this test, no such thread was ever spawned to begin with in this session, so there was nothing in flight to lose.
in_flight_work_proof.no_durable_work_discarded: creator_funding_queue is DB-backed and untouched by the stop/start cycle except via normal drain/replenish; the queue-state comparison in the individual test above (pending held at 18, retry 29->28, running 1->2, complete/expired/failed unchanged) is direct evidence no row was lost or duplicated.
